The core challenge lies in constructing conditional probabilities p(E,y) such that they define valid probability measures for almost every y. This requires careful handling of product measures and measurable transformations. In particular, the existence of a set M such that both M and its complement are thick implies pathological behavior in defining consistent conditional distributions. The failure mode arises when attempting to assign a well-defined measure to p(E,y) for all y ∈ Y, especially when the underlying σ-algebra is extended beyond standard Borel sets. The key insight is that while marginal distributions can often be constructed, the conditional distribution p(E,y) may not exist in a way compatible with measure theory unless additional regularity conditions hold. This leads to a fundamental limitation in probabilistic modeling when dealing with non-standard or irregular sets in the domain of integration.
